current.text: He signed a new contract and is set as Utah's starting point guard.
Utah has Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. for a full season and drafted Darryn Peterson. All of them take a lot of usage.

Experts expect his usage to step back and do not expect him to repeat last season's 23.6 points per game. One expects him to lose about one assist per game. He is still expected to be good and is a tier 5 point guard.

Experts think the market has dropped him too far. Lloyd finds his ESPN rank of 89 strange and doubts last season was a fluke. Another expert says a Fantrax ADP of 58 overdoes the usage drop. One speaker worries a bit about him in year four.
In an auction mock he went for 20 USD, which Josh calls a reasonable price and about what he thought George is worth.
Utah is trying to win this season and is not expected to tank or shut players down. It is projected for about 43 wins and a playoff spot, with a top 10 offense and a weak defense.

durable.text: He broke out last season. His finishing at the rim went from 54 to 65 percent.
Given how he is trending, he may be able to keep the better rim finishing.
He is not a good defender.
Turnovers are his weak category. At about 3.1 per game, he is a league outlier on the weak side.

note: The sites disagree a lot on George. Yahoo values him at 23 USD (average cost 14.7), ESPN at 3 USD (average cost 6.6), and he went for only 2 USD in our league last season. The experts think the market has dropped him too far, and a mock auction price of 20 USD was called reasonable, so 15 to 20 USD looks like a fair range. His projections help in FT% (about 87% on 6 attempts), AST, PTS and 3PM, but he hurts in TO and a little in FG%, so he fits a punt TO build best. Early in the season, check how much of the usage and the assists he keeps next to Peterson, Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.
